item.label: Static view of L-shaped brick-on-edge corner course
item.description: High-angle handheld close-up looking down at the 90-degree corner junction of a low brick wall built over bare sandy soil. Lower courses are bedded in grey mortar with some loose mortar droppings visible on the soil inside the inner corner. The top course consists of red clay bricks placed on their narrow edge without mortar (dry-laid), arranged in parallel pairs with cross-bricks (headers/stretchers) creating rectangular vertical cavities between them. At the corner junction, a small cut brick piece (bat/closer) stands vertically in the gap between the bricks, and three broken brick bats rest on the sandy soil in the upper left background. The camera holds a nearly steady framing with slight handheld drift throughout.

script: P001 states 'Unlike conventional brickwork, where bricks are laid flat, Rat-Trap Bond Masonry places bricks on their edge. This arrangement creates continuous hollow cavities within the wall' and 'Certain locations require special attention, particularly wall junctions, corners'.

background_knowledge: In Rat-Trap Bond masonry, bricks are laid on edge in a shiners-and-rowlocks (stretcher/header on edge) pattern creating internal cavities, and three-quarter or quarter bats/closers are used at corner junctions to maintain the bond.

claim_evidence.limits: Because the top course has no mortar, it illustrates the dry layout geometry rather than a completed, structurally bonded and mortared corner course.
